name: zscore_reversion_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, when the index price deviates more than 2 standard deviations from its 10-minute rolling mean, VWAP-benchmarked institutional algorithms and intraday mean-reversion quants begin fading the move aggressively — they are getting fills 20-35 spot points away from recent equilibrium, which is statistically extreme at the 5-10 minute scale. The z-score velocity filter (30-second rate of change turning back toward zero) confirms the order flow rotation has begun before the full reversion impulse lands, allowing entry in the first 5 seconds of the bounce rather than waiting for a 1-minute bar confirmation. This is a pure price-level reversion signal: NIFTY's index construction (cap-weighted, 50 liquid large caps) means deviations from the 10-minute mean are quickly arbitraged by index futures market-makers keeping spot-futures basis tight.

indicators.name: rolling_mean_120
indicators.purpose: 10-minute rolling mean (120 × 5s). Original used 60-bar 1-min = 60 minutes. Compressed to 10 min because we hold 30-120s — we want deviations from the RECENT equilibrium price, not the hour-ago mean. At 10 min, the rolling mean tracks the intraday price anchor that VWAP algorithms reference when deciding whether fills are cheap or expensive.

indicators.name: rolling_std_120
indicators.purpose: 10-minute rolling standard deviation, same window as mean. Normalizes the deviation by current session volatility so z-score threshold of 2.0 is regime-invariant. Paired with the 120-bar mean — same window, no mismatch.

indicators.name: zscore
indicators.purpose: Normalized distance from 10-min mean. Threshold 2.0 corresponds to ~20-35 NIFTY spot points in typical sessions — the level where passive market makers and VWAP algos begin aggressive counter-directional flow.

indicators.name: zscore_velocity_6
indicators.purpose: 30-second (6-bar) z-score rate of change. Confirms the reversion impulse has started: positive velocity on a deeply negative z-score means buying pressure is overpowering the downside drift. Compressed from original's 5-bar 1-min velocity (5 min) to 30s because we need real-time confirmation at 5s resolution, not 5-minute-lagged confirmation.

conditions: zscore_velocity_6 > 0 (z-score turning upward over last 30 seconds)
buy_ce.confirmation: Velocity flip from negative to positive confirms reversion impulse — not just a momentary pause but an actual order flow turn

conditions: zscore_velocity_6 < 0 (z-score turning downward over last 30 seconds)
buy_pe.confirmation: Velocity flip from positive to negative confirms sellers stepping in at overbought extreme

exit.stop_rationale: 5 option pts (~10 NIFTY spot pts at delta 0.5). At a 2-sigma deviation (20-35 spot pts from mean), the deviation can deepen by another 10 spot points on a false reversion start before either truly reversing or continuing as a trending regime — 5 pts captures this false-start risk without being stopped out by normal z-score oscillation.
exit.target_rationale: 8 option pts (~16 NIFTY spot pts). From a 2-sigma extreme on a 10-minute window (typically 20-35 spot pts deviation), the first reversion leg covers 40-60% of the total deviation; 16 spot pts captures the conservative lower end of that first leg, giving 1:1.6 risk-reward with a 5-pt stop.

filters.vix_filter: VIX < 25 — in high-vol regimes (VIX > 25), z-score extremes persist and deepen rather than reverting as institutional flows are directional not mean-reverting
filters.time_filter: 09:30-15:20 IST — 09:30 start ensures 15 minutes of data for 120-bar warmup; 15:20 cutoff avoids EOD positioning noise
filters.volume_filter: none — NIFTY index volume is noisy at 5s; signal quality from price z-score alone is sufficient
filters.trend_filter: none explicit — zscore > 2.0 threshold provides natural trend filter (if strongly trending, z-score will stay extreme but velocity will stay directional, not reversing)
filters.spread_filter: not needed — limit order execution model

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — pure price z-score is a well-known signal, but the 10-minute window with 5-second velocity confirmation is less commonly used; edge may compress as more 5s-frequency algos adopt similar triggers

adaptation_notes: Original used 60-bar 1-min lookback (60 min) on NIFTY100 stocks with Hurst exponent pre-filter. Key changes: (1) Single NIFTY index replaces stock universe — no cross-sectional screening needed. (2) Lookback compressed from 60 min to 10 min (120 bars × 5s) because we target 30-120s reversions, not 10-40 min ones — the deviation must be from the RECENT 10-minute equilibrium, not the past hour. (3) Z-score velocity compressed from 5-min to 30-second detection window to enable early entry at 5s resolution. (4) Hurst exponent filter dropped — not meaningful on a single index (NIFTY is empirically mean-reverting at intraday scale by construction). (5) VIX filter retained at same threshold (25) — same logic applies: high-vol regimes break mean-reversion across asset classes.
weaknesses: 10-minute rolling window is regime-sensitive: during strong trend days (RBI events, US market shocks), z-score will stay extreme and stop out repeatedly
Z-score velocity can give false positives during consolidation — a brief 30-second uptick in z-score velocity at a -2.5 extreme may not be a real reversion
120-bar warmup means no trades in first 10 minutes of session — misses the volatile 09:15-09:25 window which often has the cleanest mean-reversion setups after the opening spike
